title: Typing useContext and Redux Hooks
description: Learn how to type React Context consumers and Redux hooks with TypeScript.

data.text: React Context and Redux are common state management tools in React. TypeScript makes consuming them type-safe and self-documenting.
When creating a context, provide a default value that matches the context type. Always create a custom hook to consume the context so you get a clear error if the provider is missing.

data.title: Typed Context

data.text: Redux Toolkit ships with typed hooks. Use RootState and AppDispatch types so selectors and dispatch are fully typed across your app.

data.title: Typed Redux Hooks
Typed Hooks Pattern
data.text: Export typed versions of useDispatch and useSelector from a separate file. This gives you autocomplete for state slices and catches invalid dispatch calls at compile time.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Context needs a default value matching its type
Always wrap useContext in a custom hook
Redux Toolkit provides strong TypeScript inference
Export typed dispatch and selector hooks for reuse
data.takeaway: Typed context and Redux hooks make global state predictable and self-documenting.
